pools.title: Quotes
pools.description: Classic observations on craftsmanship, software, writing, and deliberate practice.
items: Simplicity is about subtracting the obvious and adding the meaningful.
First, solve the problem. Then, write the code cleanly so the next engineer can read it.
We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
Make it work, make it right, make it fast, and never sacrifice clarity for cleverness.
Programs must be written for people to read, and only incidentally for machines to execute.
Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Precision at the keyboard precedes effortless speed.
Amateurs sit and wait for inspiration; the rest of us just get up and go to work.
The secret of getting ahead is getting started with one focused step at a time.
